rule_changes.title: Bonus Points System rebalanced
rule_changes.detail: The tackle penalty is gone (players no longer lose 1 BPS for being tackled), clearances/blocks/interceptions now earn 1 BPS per three rather than per two, and goalkeeper saves are restructured: 3 BPS for an inside-box save, 2 for any other save, +1 for saving a big chance. A penalty save is 7 base +1 big chance = 8. Stated aim: reduce the overlap with defensive-contribution points and improve bonus prospects for keepers, full-backs and attackers.
rule_changes.impact: Stationary centre-backs lose bonus upside. Attacking full-backs, shot-stopping keepers and dribblers gain. Reweight any 2025/26 bonus intuition accordingly.

rule_changes.title: Defensive Contribution unchanged
rule_changes.detail: Defenders still need 10 combined clearances, blocks, interceptions and tackles. Midfielders and forwards still need 12, with ball recoveries also counting. Worth 2 points, capped at 2 per match. Goalkeepers are ineligible. The widely predicted drop from 12 to 10 for midfielders did not happen.
rule_changes.impact: High-volume defensive midfielders remain among the best points-per-million assets in the game.

rule_changes.title: Live ranks and live bonus
rule_changes.detail: Overall rank and mini-league standings now update in real time during matches, and projected bonus points appear after 20 minutes of each fixture rather than at full time.

rule_changes.title: Later gameweek lockdown
rule_changes.detail: Scores now finalise at 09:00 UK time the day after the gameweek's final match, rather than roughly an hour after the final whistle. This exists so late Opta corrections to defensive contributions and bonus can be applied.
rule_changes.impact: Do not treat Sunday-evening points as final. Provisional bonus can still move overnight.

rule_changes.title: Price changes move to midnight
rule_changes.detail: Price changes now happen once daily at 00:00 UK time, up to ±£0.1m at a time and a maximum of £0.3m in any one gameweek. Wildcard transfers are excluded from the calculation. A new official Price Change Predictor shows each player's progress toward a change as a percentage, refreshed every 15 minutes.

rule_changes.title: Chips: two sets of four, no Assistant Manager
rule_changes.detail: Wildcard, Free Hit, Bench Boost and Triple Captain, each available twice — once before the GW19 deadline (2 Jan 2027) and once after. Bench Boost and Triple Captain can be played in GW1; Wildcard and Free Hit cannot (they start GW2). First-half chips do not carry over. Only one chip per gameweek. The Assistant Manager chip from 2025/26 has been removed, along with the Manager position.

rule_changes.title: No extra AFCON transfers
rule_changes.detail: The extra December free transfers granted in 2025/26 are not being repeated — the next Africa Cup of Nations is June/July 2027, outside the season.

rule_changes.title: Free transfers still bank to five
rule_changes.detail: One free transfer per gameweek, banking up to a maximum of five. Extra transfers cost 4 points each. Sell-on fee is 50% of any profit, rounded down to the nearest £0.1m; losses are borne in full.

managers.style: Possession-heavy with a high press; Leverkusen averaged 62.1% possession.
managers.fpl_angle: The whole point of signing Geovany Quenda and Marco Palestra was to have attacking wing-backs in a back three — two brand-new defender assets with Palmer and Rogers ahead of them. Palmer inherits the ghosting inside-forward role. Prefers a dropping false nine to a target man.

managers.style: Inverted full-backs, deliberate 1v1 isolation for wide forwards.
managers.fpl_angle: Assists concentrate in the wide forwards; full-back attacking returns are suppressed because they invert rather than overlap. Semenyo had 4 assists in 3 pre-season games. Haaland remains the box finisher and takes penalties.

managers.style: Transition rather than possession; press significantly higher than Slot; full-backs push high.
managers.fpl_angle: Explicit trade-off — more chances created, more defensive vulnerability. Liverpool clean sheets look riskier than the last two seasons while attacking returns look better. Wirtz moves into a central creative role. With Salah gone and Ekitiké out until 2027, Szoboszlai and Isak absorb the dead-ball and penalty value.
avoid: Liverpool defenders as a set-and-forget clean-sheet block

managers.style: Controlled possession but a mid/low block against stronger sides rather than an aggressive press.
managers.fpl_angle: The number 10 role is described as tailor-made for Matheus Cunha. No natural left-winger in the squad. Amad may be used as an attacking right-back. Bruno Fernandes keeps penalties but a Christmas-tree variant would push him to a number 8.

managers.style: Press and possess, goalkeeper-baiting build-up. In post since March 2026.
managers.fpl_angle: Ball-playing centre-backs Senesi and Van Hecke are the build-up base, Tonali holds, Maddison and Kulusevski are the creative conduit. Solanke has said publicly the style is great for attackers. Richarlison is on penalties.

managers.system: Narrow 4-4-2 with inverted wingers, or 4-2-3-1 building to 3-2-5
managers.style: Red Bull DNA — high press, direct verticality; treats the keeper as a build-up player.
managers.fpl_angle: A fade until proven otherwise. Bruno Guimarães, Tonali, Gordon and Trippier all sold — that is penalties, corners, free-kicks and the captaincy gone in one summer. Two new goalkeepers signed means the number one spot is genuinely unsettled. Only about two weeks of preparation.
avoid: Newcastle goalkeepers until the number one is confirmed

managers.style: The Crystal Palace blueprint — wing-backs provide all the width, elite set-piece routines.
managers.fpl_angle: Neco Williams and Ola Aina are the systemic beneficiaries. Glasner's Palace were one of the best set-piece sides in the league; watch for the same pattern at the City Ground. Gibbs-White (15 PL goals last season) is the focal 10.

managers.style: Aggressive counter-press; the first line pushes opponents wide so wing-backs and wide centre-backs trap on the touchline.
managers.fpl_angle: Muñoz and Mitchell are explicitly the beneficiaries — Palace's best performances come when the wing-backs are unleashed early. One of the central midfielders stays anchored, which caps Wharton's attacking ceiling.

managers.system: Gegenpressing, even more aggressive than Iraola
managers.style: Vertical intent, players occupying inside spaces, energetic full-backs as the width and main creative outlet.
managers.fpl_angle: Truffert is the model full-back for this system — 103 tackles, 188 possessions won and 141 crosses last season. Older legs (Adam Smith 35, Christie 31) are at risk. Bournemouth have lost both Senesi and Semenyo.

managers.style: Front-foot high press — a sharp break from Silva's mid-block.
managers.fpl_angle: The biggest gamble of the eight appointments: no meaningful senior management experience beyond Real Madrid Castilla. Treat Fulham assets as high variance until the style settles. Gonzalo García arrives as the striker and first-choice penalty taker.

managers.style: Survival specialist, limited tactician but proven at keeping small clubs up.
managers.fpl_angle: Around ten signings made. Jack Clarke on penalties.

managers.style: Took Coventry up playing on the front foot.
managers.fpl_angle: Haji Wright on penalties; Grimes takes set pieces.
Oli McBurnie on penalties. Jack Butland signed but has an arm injury.

Arsenal.note: Sources conflict — RotoWire has Gyökeres first, AllAboutFPL still lists Saka. Treat as not fully nailed on.

Aston Villa.note: The biggest quiet role upgrade in the league — Rogers, Tielemans and Digne all left, so Buendía inherits penalties, corners and free-kicks.

Brentford.note: Igor Thiago converted 8 of 9 last season. One of only four clubs with genuinely clear-cut duties.

Liverpool.note: Sources split on the order between Szoboszlai and Isak.

Manchester City.note: Haaland 6 of 6 in all competitions. Clear-cut.

Newcastle United.note: All previous takers sold. Genuinely unsettled.

watchlist: Liverpool are a different team — Salah gone, Ekitiké out until 2027, no winger signed, and Iraola trades control for chaos. More chances, worse clean-sheet security.
Alonso's Chelsea wing-backs (Quenda, Palestra) are two brand-new attacking-defender assets if he commits to the back three.
Buendía is the biggest quiet role upgrade in the league — he inherits penalties, corners and free-kicks at Villa.
Newcastle are a fade until proven otherwise: four senior leaders sold, two weeks of preparation, two keepers competing.
Glasner at Forest and Sage at Palace both mean wing-backs. Neco Williams, Ola Aina, Muñoz and Mitchell are the systemic beneficiaries.
The BPS rebalance quietly downgrades stationary centre-backs and upgrades attacking full-backs and shot-stopping keepers.
